# Best rechargeable AA batteries

**Short answer:** For most people, Panasonic Eneloop (standard or Pro) is the safest pick, and IKEA LADDA is the cheap alternative. Which Eneloop depends on the device.

## My picks

**Best overall for high-drain devices (flashes, controllers, flashlights): Panasonic Eneloop Pro AA**
- 2,600 mAh, keeps 85% of its charge after 1 year, and is rated for about 500 recharges. Digital Camera World ranks it #1 and reports 100% reliability in its flash testing. [1]
- The tradeoff is fewer cycles and a higher price (roughly $4.50 per cell per GearLab). [2]
- I don't have a direct product link from the search results. Digital Camera World's guide links to Adorama, Amazon, and Newegg listings: https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries

**Best for longevity and storage: Panasonic Eneloop (standard) AA**
- 2,000 mAh, but rated for up to 2,100 recharges and about 70% charge retained after 10 years. [1] It's a good fit for remotes, clocks, and emergency kits. Buy through the same guide above.

**Best budget: IKEA LADDA**
- Charge-Test's lab measurements found the LADDA 2450 mAh cells nearly match the Eneloop Pro (about 2,350 mAh at a 1A load), and the 1,900 mAh version sits just below the standard Eneloop. [3] Its testing suggests the cells are Eneloop-based, though IKEA has never confirmed this.
- The US IKEA page lists the 1,900 mAh AA 4-pack at $9.99, with a 4.7/5 rating across 1,009 reviews: https://www.ikea.com/us/en/p/ladda-rechargeable-battery-hr06-aa-1-2v-00509814/ [4]
- I couldn't confirm the 2450 mAh version on IKEA's US site. GearLab lists it at $7.99, but its pricing is in-store and may not match the US listing. [2]

**Best for bulk: Tenergy Premium PRO AA, 2,800 mAh, 20-pack ($42.99)**
- Rated for 1,200 cycles, with 85% retained after 1 year. [5]
- Buy: https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-premium-pro-aa-2800mah-20-pack
- This source only had Tenergy in its records and didn't compare it with Eneloop or LADDA, and its links are affiliate links. Treat it as a reasonable option, not a verified winner.

**For devices that need a true 1.5V:** Digital Camera World recommends the EBL 1.5V Li-ion AA, since NiMH cells run at 1.2V and some devices read that as low. [1]

## Charger
If you need one, the Tenergy TN480U 8-bay charger ($23.99) handles AA and AAA NiMH cells, with USB-C input and a per-slot LCD. It doesn't include a power adapter. [5]
Buy: https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-tn480u-8-bay-nimh-charger

## A caution on the sources
Two Frame & Focal articles (one of which I've left out) reported very poor results for Amazon Basics cells. Some of their details are inconsistent with other sources, such as the Eneloop Pro capacity figures, so I wouldn't lean on them. GearLab, by contrast, recommends Amazon Basics only for low-drain uses like remotes and clocks. [2]

Sources:
[1] https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries
[2] https://gearlab.io/best-rechargeable-batteries-for-household-devices/
[3] https://charge-test.com/ikea-ladda-batteries-review-still-the-best-budget-aa-aaa-rechargeable-in-2026/
[4] https://www.ikea.com/us/en/p/ladda-rechargeable-battery-hr06-aa-1-2v-00509814/
[5] https://dealectric.com/answers/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries-2026-tests-capacity-self-discharge-panasonic-enel

What will you use them in? I can narrow this to one pick.
